Surface candidate block hashes on lookup misses so callers can fetch missing blocks on demand.

categories.name: indexes
why: P2 because it eliminates the long-standing mutual exclusion between txindex and block pruning.
Pruned node operators gain transaction lookup capabilities without needing to store hundreds of gigabytes of historical blocks.

why: P3 because it informs callers which pruned block to fetch when a transaction is missing.
Also adds the first indexed block height to getindexinfo to distinguish partial indexes.

result.summary: This PR lifts the mutual exclusivity between txindex and pruned mode, building on the packed block hash references introduced in #35531. TxIndex can now identify the block hash of a transaction even if the underlying block file has been deleted, returning the block hash on lookup so callers can retrieve the block via getblockfrompeer. It also introduces partial history support so a txindex can be initialized on an already pruned node without redownloading earlier history.
result.problem: Previously, running txindex required retaining the entire raw block history on disk, completely barring pruned nodes from indexing transactions or locating which historical blocks contained specific transactions.

open_concerns: arejula27 asked whether AllowPrune() and AllowPartialHistory() in BaseIndex should be combined into a single enum to enforce that partial history implies prune support.
arejula27 questioned whether candidate pruned block hashes should be returned as structured data in RPC responses rather than embedded in error strings.
resolved_concerns: ajtowns and mzumsande inquired about behavior on already pruned nodes; author updated the design to support starting from an already pruned height and exposed first_block_height.

categories.name: indexes
categories.evidence: Modifies BaseIndex and TxIndex to allow running under block pruning and starting sync from a non-genesis block.
categories.rationale: Enabling txindex on pruned nodes has been a long-requested feature that removes a major barrier for users who cannot afford hundreds of gigabytes of block storage. Following #35531's decoupling of txindex entries from raw block file positions, this change delivers durable value to index users by making txindex usable on resource-constrained nodes.

categories.name: rpc
categories.evidence: Updates getrawtransaction, gettxoutproof, rest_tx, and getindexinfo to handle pruned lookup misses and partial index status.
categories.rationale: Surfacing candidate pruned block hashes in getrawtransaction and gettxoutproof enables callers to retrieve missing blocks via getblockfrompeer. Adding first_block_height to getindexinfo provides necessary transparency for partial index instances.

result.card: This PR allows running txindex alongside block pruning and enables starting an index on an already pruned node. When a requested transaction resides in a pruned block, the index returns the containing block hash so users or downstream tools can fetch the block with getblockfrompeer and retry. The work resolves a long-standing limitation where txindex required full block storage. Concept support is strong across several reviewers, and the code is ready for review with ongoing discussion around whether candidate block hashes should be surfaced as structured RPC data.
